# Overview 

This post details the experimental design plans for sampling acute stress survival of Manchester Hardening experiment oysters.  

*Note that I will keep updating this post as we get more information on sample size and specific protocols.*  

## Oysters 

Oysters will be collected from Manchester on Friday, August 15th and transported to UW campus by Mac.    

The oysters will be held in red seed bags (n=20 total bags) that correspond to 10 families from 2 treatment groups (10 x 2 = 20). These are our "family treatment groups".    

Each bag will contain a waterproof paper label with the family and treatment information.   

We will see how many oysters are surviving from each family treatment group to update and finalize sample size.  

#### Family treatment groups: 

The oysters will be identified by a family + a treatment group from our hardening experiment. This will be something like "YC24-087" (family) and "High" or "Control" (treatment). Note that the treatment refers to the hardening treatment, *NOT* the treatment for survival or resazurin testing. These assays will run at a stressful temperature for all oysters as in the standard lab protocols.  

I will label the bags with numbers 1-20 to make labeling easy. I'll create a metadata sheet with the family group information assigned to each number.  

#### Sample size: 

This will be based on how many oysters are sampled. I will update this as we go. I expect at least n=10 per family group (~200 oysters). We are going to proceed with survival assays as the main lab test.  

## Survival 

#### Schedule: 

August 17-20 (ish): Round 1 of n=4 oysters per bag, n=80 oysters total 
August 24-27 (ish): Round 2 of n=4 oysters per bag, n=80 oysters total 
August 31-Sept 3 (ish): Round 3 of n=4 oysters per bag, n=80 oysters total 

#### Materials needed:  

- Numbered plastic cups (n=80 per round)
- Seawater (Instant Ocean adjusted to ambient levels) 
- Seawater table running for temperature control 

#### Base protocol: 

- Pre heat the water table such that cups in the water table reach 36°C (may need to have the table heater set at 38-40°C)
- Obtain n=4 oysters per bag per round (n=80 oysters per round)
- Place oysters into numbered cups, being sure to record which bag is in represented in each cup (e.g.,  Bags 1-20). Labels are based on the label in each bag of oysters. 
- Fill cups with seawater and ensure each oyster is alive. 
- Record which oysters are dead in the morning and evening of each day for 3-5 days until ~80-90% of oysters have died. 
- Record the temperature in 5 cups in the water table each time mortality is assessed and write down the temperature readings.  
- Send all data to Ariana. 
- Repeat until we get through at least 12-16 oysters per bag.  

#### Data sheets that will need to be recorded: 

All data will need to be recorded for each "round".   

1. Temperature recorded in n=5 cups at each sampling point   
2. Alive/dead oysters at each time point   
3. The time of the start of the experiment and time of each sampling time point   
4. A metadata sheet that contains the cup number, bag number, round, and any notes
